desc: Design algorithm: edge keep/cut forced by child subtree size mod K (cut if ≡ 0, keep otherwise); validate kept components are K-vertex paths

Prove correctness sketch: at most one path crosses any edge, so subtree size mod K forces the decision; residue argument (sizes increase by 1 mod K down a kept chain from a ≡0 root) shows degree ≤ 2 implies component size exactly K
Implement full program: fast stdin parsing, adjacency construction, iterative postorder subtree sizes (no recursion), kept-edge marking, DSU component sizes + kept-degree check, output Yes/No

Verify mentally against samples and edge cases: Sample 1 → Yes (components {1,2},{3,4},{5,6}), Sample 2 → No (vertex 3 gets kept-degree 3); K=1 cuts all edges → always Yes; N=1 → Yes iff tree is a path; singleton components impossible for K>1 since size ≡ 1 ≢ 0 forces the parent edge to be kept
